comp_010:n1.prompt:
You are helping me generate a privacy policy and terms of service using {{vendor}}, our compliance-automation platform, ahead of publishing and DPA setup. Please do the following:

1. If you don't already have it, ask me for: my company/legal entity name, primary domain, product description, jurisdictions we operate in or sell into, and any known data types we collect (e.g., customer PII, payment data, usage analytics).
2. Using your configured credentials, access {{vendor}}'s Policy Center and use its policy creation capability (the same operation Drata exposes as POST /openapi/reference/v2/tag/Policies/) to create two new policy records: one for our Privacy Policy and one for our Terms of Service, selecting the lawyer-grade template library entries closest to our business type.
3. Populate each template's editable fields (company name, domain, data types, contact/DPO info, jurisdiction-specific clauses like GDPR/CCPA) using the inputs I gave you, and save as a draft version — do not publish or finalize yet.
4. Enable versioning and set up an approval workflow in {{vendor}} routing each draft to legal/counsel for review, and configure per-employee acceptance tracking so we can later confirm staff have read and accepted the policies.
5. Compile a summary listing: the two draft policy names/IDs, their current version numbers, who they're routed to for approval, and any template fields you couldn't fill because information was missing.

Done looks like: both draft policies exist in {{vendor}} with versioning and an approval workflow pending counsel review, and acceptance tracking is configured but not yet triggered. Do not mark either policy as final, approved, or published — that requires counsel sign-off, so stop for human sign-off once drafts and routing are ready. Report back with the draft names/IDs, version numbers, approval routing status, and the list of missing inputs, if any.

comp_010:n2.prompt:
You are helping me prepare and track outside counsel review of our privacy policy and Data Processing Addendum (DPA) before we publish them. This is a policy-gate step: you must prepare everything needed for review but must not approve, sign, or publish anything yourself.

First, ask me for anything you need that isn't already available: our current draft privacy policy and DPA documents (or their file/document locations), our subprocessor list, the name/contact of the outside counsel or law firm reviewing this, our target jurisdictions/data-protection laws (e.g., GDPR, CCPA), and our target publish date.

Then do the following:
1. Compile a clean review package: the draft privacy policy, DPA, and subprocessor list, plus a short cover memo listing open questions (e.g., specific clauses needing legal judgment, jurisdictions in scope, any recent product changes affecting data handling).
2. Draft an email to counsel requesting review, including the package, our target timeline, and specific questions we want addressed.
3. Create a tracking checklist noting: date sent, counsel contact, expected turnaround, and status (pending/received/changes requested/approved).
4. Since this is an async, person-driven step, note in your report that you cannot complete or verify the review yourself — someone must periodically check with counsel or their portal/email for a response, and you should prompt me to confirm when a reply arrives so you can log it and prepare any requested edits.

Do not tell me to sign, approve, accept terms, or submit the documents for publication — that decision belongs to counsel and me. Once the package and email draft are ready, stop for human sign-off and report back with: the compiled review package, the draft outreach email, the tracking checklist, and a clear note that the legal adequacy review remains a human step until counsel responds.

comp_010:n3.prompt:
You are helping me publish our finalized Privacy Policy and DPA pages to our live website using {{vendor}}, an edge-platform host that deploys static sites from Git with global CDN caching.

Before starting, ask me for anything you don't already have: (1) the path or repo location of our website project, (2) the file names/paths for the Privacy Policy and DPA pages (assume they are already legally reviewed and finalized — do not draft or edit their legal content), and (3) our production domain name.

Actions to take:
1. Confirm the Privacy Policy and DPA pages exist in the site's source (e.g., under /privacy and /dpa or similar routes) and are linked from the site footer or navigation if that's part of our existing template.
2. Connect the repo to {{vendor}} (or confirm it's already connected) so future Git pushes trigger automatic deploys — no manual build configuration should be needed.
3. Deploy the current build using the platform's CLI, invoking the equivalent of `{{vendor}} deploy --allow-anonymous` from the project's working directory, using your configured credentials.
4. After deploy, verify the live URLs for the Privacy Policy and DPA pages return 200 status and render correctly, and confirm they're served via the platform's CDN (check response headers or the deploy summary for edge/cache confirmation).
5. Confirm the pages are reachable at our production domain (not just a preview/staging URL) — if custom domain wiring is needed, note it but treat DNS/domain configuration as out of scope unless already set up.

Done looks like: both pages are live at their production URLs, loading correctly, linked from the site, and served through the CDN.

Report back: the live URLs for both pages, the deploy status/ID from {{vendor}}, and any issues found (broken links, missing pages, domain not yet wired) that need my attention.

comp_010:n4.prompt:
You are helping me set up the DPA e-signature flow for our privacy paperwork using {{vendor}}, a legal-ops e-signature platform. If you don't already have it, ask me for: our company/product name, the finalized DPA document or template text, the list of signer roles (e.g., our authorized signer plus the customer's authorized signer), and our domain for embedding the signing flow on our site.

Goal: configure {{vendor}} so customers can request and complete a legally binding DPA signature, embedded in our app/site or sent via email, with proper routing across multiple recipients.

Actions:
1. Using your configured credentials, access {{vendor}}'s API or dashboard.
2. Create a DPA envelope template populated with our DPA document and the correct signer fields/roles in the right signing order.
3. Configure the flow so it can be triggered programmatically (via {{vendor}}'s documented API) to generate, populate, and send the DPA to a customer's signer(s), with support for multiple recipients and routing.
4. Set up embedding of the signing experience within our own app or website, using {{vendor}}'s embed capability, pointing at our domain.
5. Create a webhook to receive e-signature workflow events (e.g., sent, viewed, completed) so we can track DPA status internally.
6. Test the full flow end-to-end with a sample recipient to confirm the envelope generates correctly, routes to the right signer(s), and the webhook fires on completion.

Done looks like: a working DPA template in {{vendor}}, an API-triggerable send/route flow, an embedded signing experience wired to our site, and a webhook receiving completion events — all verified with a test send.

Report back: confirm what was configured (template name/ID, webhook target, embed location), the result of the test signature, and any manual dashboard steps I still need to review before going live.

comp_010:n5.prompt:
You are helping me maintain our public subprocessor list as part of our privacy paperwork. We use {{vendor}} for project management and shared docs, and I want the subprocessor list maintained there alongside our other privacy documentation.

Please do the following:
1. Ask me for: (a) my company/domain name, (b) the current list of subprocessors we use (name, purpose/function, data types processed, and country/region of processing) if I haven't already given you one, and (c) the URL or location of our published privacy policy/DPA page so the subprocessor list can be linked or referenced consistently.
2. In {{vendor}}, create (or update if one exists) a shared doc titled something like "Subprocessor List" organized in a clear table format with columns: Subprocessor Name, Purpose, Data Processed, Location/Region, and Date Added/Last Reviewed.
3. Populate the doc with the subprocessors I provide, and structure it so new entries can be added easily going forward.
4. Set up the doc to live alongside our other privacy/compliance project materials in {{vendor}} so it's easy to find and update.
5. Draft a short note or comment in the doc explaining the update cadence I intend to follow (e.g., reviewed whenever a new vendor is added or quarterly), based on what I tell you.
6. Do not publish anything externally or notify customers — this step is only about creating and organizing the internal, maintained source-of-truth list.

When done, report back with: the location/link of the doc in {{vendor}}, a summary of the subprocessors currently listed, and confirmation that the doc is organized and ready to be kept current. If any subprocessor details are missing or unclear, flag them for me rather than guessing.
